sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant has falsely been implicated in the present case and he has nothing to do with the alleged offence.
Expeditious culmination of trial is not a seeming fate and no fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the appellant behind the bars.
He, therefore, prays that benefit of bail may be granted to the appellant.
3. Per contra, learned learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsel for the complainant has opposed the bail application.

4. Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant and perused the material available on record.
5.

Have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the challan papers available on record more particularly, the FIR, the statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 & 164 of the Cr.P.C.
6.
The FIR came to be lodged by none other than the victim herself, who is a grown up widow lady of 40 years and having three children.
Even in the FIR, she admits that she was in good terms with the petitioner.

As per the allegations levelled in the FIR, when she was taking bath in her house, the [2024:RJ-JD:2197] (3 of 4) [CRLAS-2461/2023] accused came there and took naked pictures of her and whereafter on several occasions, she was subjected to rape by him.
A serious discrepancy can be observed in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.

Now, coming to the accused, his conduct in responding on Whats App and sending her pictures to other persons cannot be appreciated rather deserves to be deprecated but at the same time, this cannot be ignored that the victim is a 40 years old married lady and there was no circumstance under which she had to submit her before the petitioner for fornication.

Even a critical scrutiny of the FIR and her statement do not revealing that at what point of time the first incident of seducing her took place and if it is so then it is not comprehensible that what prevented her to lodge the FIR promptly with regard to the alleged obnoxious behavior of the accused.
Prima facie, there is a substance in the submission of learned counsel that taking nude pictures in her bathroom by the petitioner is a false pretext.

It is out of the common prudence to believe that the accused who is residing in a different village then how he visited the house of the victim in a broad daylight where she was taking bath in an open place that too without clothing; so as to make a circumstance for the accused to snap her shots.

If the contents of the FIR and the statements of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
are compared with one another, one can observed several incongruity therein.

Be that as it may,
after completion of the investigation, keeping the petitioner behind the bars would not be justifiable as [2024:RJ-JD:2197] (4 of 4) [CRLAS-2461/2023] there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.

In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the Ganpatram Jakhar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:2197) on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76727990/
2 benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.

sentences.text: 7. Initially all the offence attributed were bailable, therefor, the Investigating Agency had obtained the bail bonds of the appellant, however after edition of Section 3 of the SC/ST Act and Section 308 of the IPC, the appellant was arrested and now he is languishing in jail, there appears no reasonable ground for further incarceration, as trial would take a long time to conclude thus, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
8. Consequently, the instant appeal is allowed.
The impugned order dated 09.10.2023 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Cases, Merta in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.202/2023 is hereby quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Cases, Merta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is ordered that the accused-appellant, named in the cause title, arrested in connection with aforesaid FIR, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.
25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court with the stipulation to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so (FARJAND ALI),J 102-Mamta/-
